thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Routing anomaly detected: sudden spike in traffic to cheapest_variant_v2-quant in us-west-2. Metric: quality_regression_alert (customer-facing evals increased failure rate by 18% over 2 mins). Auto-page triggered.

maria: acked. I'm taking pager. Can someone grab a quick impact estimate?

jason: on it, looking at eval delta now. early read: batch of top-prod requests got routed to quantized cheap variant due to a policy priority inversion in the budget-led routing rule.

sarah: Support sees uptick in customer error reports from AcmeCorp (5 complaints in last 10m). They say hallucinations + truncated completions.

lee: timeline? did the policy change just roll? I didn't see any config deploys in the console.

jason: no manual deploys. Looks like the autoscaling/fallback policy evaluation returned a cheaper-compatible flag when sequence length > 512. The comparator mistakenly matched variant with compatible_latency but unknown quality profile.

maria: ok mitigation options: 1) disable budget-led routing globally 2) pin AcmeCorp to stable-llama-v1 3) add emergency quality threshold to policy engine. I'll do 1 and 2 immediately.

jason: agree. Quick command to disable cost routing via admin API:

```
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/routing/policies/disable \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"policy_id":"budget-led","reason":"emergency disable - quality regressions"}'
```

maria: issuing now.

maria: @deploy-bot please apply policy disable rollout-001 - emergency.

deploy-bot: policy rollout-001 started by maria. Target: disable budget-led routing. Estimated time: <30s.

maria: also patching customer route for AcmeCorp to stable pinned model: stable-llama-v1 (region us-west-2). Command:

```
# pin route
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/customers/AcmeCorp/route \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"stable-llama-v1","scope":"customer","duration":"1h","reason":"emergency pin due to quality regression"}'
```

jason: I'm streaming the eval logs. sample request that triggered regression:

```
REQ id=xyz123 prompt_len=620 route=budget-led matched_variant=cheapest_variant_v2-quant quality_score=0.42 avg_expected=0.88
```

jason: note matched_variant had quant suffix and no verified eval profile. The routing engine incorrectly considered quantized variant compatible because latency budgets were being prioritized too aggressively.

maria: deploy-bot shows policy disabled. Confirming traffic shift...

deploy-bot: rollout-001 complete. budget-led policy status: DISABLED.

oncall-ml: I see 92% of affected traffic now pinned or routed to stable variants. Latency bump ~ 20ms, but quality metrics trending back up.

sarah: support: informing AcmeCorp CSM & logging escalation. Customers asked for ETA on full recovery. We can say mitigation in progress and that we pinned their routing.

lee: can we also block region fallback for the next 30m? If the cheaper variant was in a different region, fallback logic might be shunting requests cross-region.
jason: good call. I'll temporarily disable cross-region fallback in routing policies.

jason: disabling cross-region fallback now via console (UI action recorded).

maria: quick postmortem notes we need in incident: root cause = policy prioritization bug that allowed 'cost' score to override 'quality' when sequence length heuristic flipped compatibility. Contributing factor = missing guard rails for unverified quantized variants.

jason: adding mitigation list: emergency disable of budget-led, pinning high-risk customers, disabling cross-region fallback, and adding a preflight verification step in policy engine for unknown variants.

maria: Sarah, please confirm customer communications block. Lee, can you own follow-up changelist to add a quality threshold >0.7 for any auto-fallback or cost-driven variant?

lee: yes, I'll draft the CL and aim for a review within 4 hours. Will include unit tests around priority tie-breakers.

sarah: Customer comms: sent initial notice to AcmeCorp support + CSM. They acknowledged and appreciate the quick pin. They'll open a ticket if further issues.

maria: handing off to jason in 25m for monitoring phase. I'll stay on for 5 more to supervise alert thresholds.
jason: taking the mid-window handoff. I'll monitor quality_regression_alert and live evals for the next 2 hours.

maria: final quick action items captured:
- emergency disable budget-led routing (done)
- pin affected customers to stable-llama-v1 (done for AcmeCorp)
- disable cross-region fallback (done)
- deploy follow-up CL to add quality threshold & preflight checks (owner: lee)
- create regression test that simulates sequence-length heuristic (owner: jason)

maria: closing pager for now — keeping incident thread open for postmortem. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
